personality_temperament.claim: Majestic, supreme, highly volatile when challenged, yet deeply reflective and strategic. Operates with detachment from immediate mortal suffering while maintaining ultimate cosmic sovereignty (Iliad 8.1–28).

values_priorities.claim: Cosmic order (Themis), institutional justice (Dikē), sanctity of oaths (Zeus Horkios), protection of suppliants (Zeus Xenios), and preservation of supreme authority (timē).

decision_patterns.claim: Weighs competing divine demands on golden scales (kērostasia); grants requests based on historical charis or grand narrative plans (Dios Boulē); enforces decrees through irresistible force (thunderbolt) or binding nods (Iliad 1.528–530).

conflicting_priorities.claim: When personal affection for mortals (e.g., Sarpedon, Hector) conflicts with fated destiny (Moira), Zeus yields to Moira to prevent divine anarchy and maintain pantheonic consensus (Iliad 16.431–461).

methods_of_action.claim: Lightning bolts, sending omens (eagles, thunder), psychological illumination or delusion (atē), sending dream messengers (Hypnos, Iris), and imperial decrees.

limits_exceptions.claim: Bound by Moira; cannot alter past events; subject to temporary erotic deception (Seduction of Zeus in Iliad 14).
